newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Andy Haden slams shield advertisement.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Andy Haden slams shield advertisement.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 1 - Former Auckland captain Andy Haden is astonished the Auckland Rugby Football Union (ARFU) has billed their match against North Harbour as a Ranfurly Shield fixture, NZPA reported on Tuesday.
The ARFU caused a stir yesterday by taking out a newspaper advertisement for the October 12 match against North Harbour at Eden Park.
The union billed the game as a shield match even though Waikato are the Ranfurly Shield holders. Auckland challenge for the shield in Hamilton on Friday night.

"I would suggest it has been done by someone who's never put on a pair of boots, has never smelled the liniment and doesn't know what's involved in winning a shield match or a test match," the former All Blacks lock said.
"As an exercise in providing ammunition for your opposition, it comes into the category of landmining your own dressing room.
"John Boe (Waikato coach) can stay at home. His team talk has been written for him."
The idea for the advertisement came from ARFU chief executive Peter Scutts as a response to moderate crowds this season at Eden Park.
"I wanted people to be thinking about our game with Harbour now rather than looking at the idea next week," Scutts said.
"I wanted to do something a bit different and to provoke a reaction and find out why Aucklanders come to rugby matches."
Scutts said the presumptuous advertisement was not aimed at Waikato or the Ranfurly Shield. It was a marketing tool to try to raise crowd numbers at Eden Park.
